config.title: useMediaQuery

intro.title: useMediaQuery
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a responsive React component that changes its background color based on the screen width. You will learn how to use the useMediaQuery custom hook to detect and respond to changes in media conditions, such as viewport size. The main technologies involved are React hooks, JavaScript, and CSS media queries. This beginner-friendly project will help you understand how to make your applications adapt dynamically to different devices.
intro.usecase: The useMediaQuery hook is essential for creating responsive interfaces that adapt to different screen sizes in real-world applications. Developers use it to conditionally render components like navigation menus that switch between hamburger menus on mobile and full menus on desktop. In e-commerce sites, product grids might display fewer items per row on smaller screens, while dashboards could hide secondary panels on tablets. This pattern also enables dynamic theming based on user preferences, such as switching to dark mode when the system preference changes.

objectives: Implement the useMediaQuery hook to detect viewport size changes
Apply media query conditions to control component rendering behavior
Construct responsive UI components that adapt to different screen sizes
Initialize media query state with default values for different breakpoints
Manipulate component styles based on media query evaluation results
Integrate useMediaQuery with conditional rendering patterns
Update component state in response to media query changes

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are correctly added at the top of the file.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Make sure to return a <div> element.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: A functional component named App exists and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it's named 'App' and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a function named App that returns a <div>.

steps.title: Define the useMediaQuery custom hook
steps.instruction: Define a custom hook named useMediaQuery that takes a query string parameter.
steps.hint: Create a function that starts with 'use' and accepts a query parameter. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: A custom hook function named useMediaQuery is defined with a query parameter.
successCriteria: The code contains a function named useMediaQuery that accepts a query parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined a function named useMediaQuery that accepts a query parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useMediaQuery hook isn't properly defined. Check that you've created a function with the correct name and parameter.

steps.title: Initialize state in the custom hook
steps.instruction: Inside the useMediaQuery function, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'matches' that tracks whether the media query matches, initializing it to false.
steps.hint: Call useState with an initial value of false and destructure the returned array to get the state variable and setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useMediaQuery function will have a state variable 'matches' initialized to false using useState.
successCriteria: The useMediaQuery function contains a useState call that initializes a 'matches' state variable to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to create a state variable named 'matches' initialized to false inside the useMediaQuery function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the useMediaQuery function, use useState to create a state variable called 'matches' with an initial value of false.

steps.title: Add useEffect to listen for media changes
steps.instruction: Inside the useMediaQuery function, add a useEffect hook that will create a MediaQueryList object and add an event listener for media changes.
steps.hint: Use useEffect to run side effects. Inside it, create a MediaQueryList using window.matchMedia with a query string, then add an event listener to it that updates state when changes occur.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useMediaQuery hook now includes a useEffect that sets up a media query listener.
successCriteria: useEffect is added to the useMediaQuery function, creates a MediaQueryList object, and adds an event listener for changes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure useEffect includes both adding and removing the event listener, and creates the MediaQueryList object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Add a useEffect hook inside useMediaQuery that creates a MediaQueryList and sets up an event listener for changes.

steps.title: Return the match state from the hook
steps.instruction: Make your useMediaQuery custom hook return the current matches state value.
steps.hint: At the end of the hook function, use a return statement to return the matches variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useMediaQuery hook will now return the current match value, making it usable in components.
successCriteria: The useMediaQuery hook returns the matches state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning the matches variable from the hook function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook should return the matches state value. Add a return statement at the end of the function.

steps.title: Use the custom hook in the App component
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, call the useMediaQuery hook with the media query string '(max-width: 768px)' and store its return value in a variable named isMobile.
steps.hint: Call the hook like you would any other React hook: const isMobile = useMediaQuery('(max-width: 768px)');
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: calling a custom hook
const isLoggedIn = useAuth();
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a variable isMobile that holds the boolean result of the media query.
successCriteria: The useMediaQuery hook is called with '(max-width: 768px)' and its return value is assigned to a variable named isMobile inside the App component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling useMediaQuery with the exact string '(max-width: 768px)' and storing the result in a variable named isMobile.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook call is missing or incorrect. Inside the App component, you need to call useMediaQuery('(max-width: 768px)') and assign it to const isMobile.

steps.title: Display the match status in JSX
steps.instruction: In your App component's return statement, add a paragraph that displays whether the screen is mobile-sized based on the matches value from useMediaQuery.
steps.hint: Use the matches variable returned by useMediaQuery in a JSX expression to show a message like 'Screen is mobile-sized: true' or 'Screen is mobile-sized: false'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component returns JSX that displays the current matches value from useMediaQuery in a paragraph.
successCriteria: The App component returns a paragraph element that contains the matches value from useMediaQuery in a JSX expression.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying the matches value from useMediaQuery in a paragraph element. Check that you're using the correct variable name and JSX syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component doesn't yet display the match status. Add a paragraph element that shows the matches value from useMediaQuery using JSX expression syntax.

steps.title: Add visual feedback for different screen sizes
steps.instruction: In the App component's JSX, add a div that conditionally applies a CSS class based on the matches state from useMediaQuery. Use a ternary operator to set className to 'screen-large' when matches is true, and 'screen-small' when false.
steps.hint: You can use a ternary operator directly in the className attribute: className={matches ? 'screen-large' : 'screen-small'}
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will render a div that visually changes appearance based on screen size, using CSS classes applied conditionally through the matches state.
successCriteria: A div element is added with className set using a ternary operator that references the matches variable, applying 'screen-large' when true and 'screen-small' when false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a div, but check that the className uses the matches variable with a ternary operator to switch between 'screen-large' and 'screen-small'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional className wasn't properly implemented. Make sure to add a div with className={matches ? 'screen-large' : 'screen-small'}.

steps.title: Test the responsive behavior
steps.instruction: Resize your browser window to see the content update based on screen width.
steps.hint: Make the browser window narrower than 768px and wider than 768px to see the text change.
steps.expectedOutcome: When you resize the browser window, the text 'Matches: Yes' changes to 'Matches: No' (and vice versa) based on whether the screen width is at least 768px.
successCriteria: The text updates in real time as you resize the browser window.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: The hook is set up, but make sure you're resizing the browser window to see the text change.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook might not be working. Check that you're resizing the browser window and that the media query is set to '(min-width: 768px)'.
